issues.title: Disprove 00000003470: clique-tree embedding count misses K2 orderings
issues.body:
The complete chordal graph K2 has two perfect elimination orderings but only one maximal clique. Its unique maximal-clique tree is a single vertex, with one combinatorial planar embedding. The claimed product of embedding counts is therefore one rather than the true elimination-ordering count two. The report states the standard embedding equivalence convention and the distinction between labeled orderings and graph-automorphism classes.

The personal submission includes LaTeX, a visually verified two-page PDF, and a public pinned Lean 4.19.0/Mathlib project. Lean verifies actual chordality, the PEO successor condition and permutation count, unique maximal clique and clique graph, actual incident-neighbor rotations and their count, and the mismatch. Final full lake build passed; printed theorem audits use only standard propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. No admitted results or custom axioms.

issues.title: Disprove conjecture 00000004227: a triangle has one 2-tree but chromatic value minus six
issues.body:
## Conjecture 00000004227

**Result: Disproof.** The flag complex of K3 is a filled triangle with exactly one spanning 2-tree. Its clique number is 3 and its chromatic polynomial is q(q-1)(q-2), so the specified negative evaluation gives -6, not 1. Absolute-value or parity correction gives 6, and the opposite positive argument gives 0; neither equals the tree count. In fact every negative integer evaluation has absolute value at least 6.

## Scope

This refutes the stated unit conversion from a flag-complex 2-tree count to the chromatic-polynomial evaluation at the negative point determined by clique number minus two. The example has dimension exactly 2. Its unique tree has trivial integral first homology, so ordinary counting and the usual squared torsion-order weighting both give 1. The proof covers sign conventions and all negative integer points; it does not posit an unspecified linear combination of evaluations or a different normalization.

## Formalization and actual verification

Lean constructs the actual complete SimpleGraph on three vertices, its clique complex and clique number. An equivalence between proper colorings and embeddings proves the polynomial counting property for every natural number of colors, and polynomial uniqueness is also proved. Actual simplicial boundary maps over Q define the supported-chain spanning 2-tree predicate; Lean classifies all face selections and proves its count is 1. It proves the prescribed evaluation is -6, the positive-point and absolute-value comparisons, and the stronger inequality at every negative integer. The direct integer filling establishing trivial torsion is explained on paper, separately from the Q-linear formalization.

The submitted source passed a fresh Lean **4.19.0** `lake build` with warnings treated as errors, and `lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true Main.lean`. Mathlib and its transitive dependencies are pinned in the public-Git Lake manifest. Only verified dependency artifacts were reused; the submitted project itself was rebuilt in a fresh directory. Printed axiom dependencies are standard foundational axioms; no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, or custom axiom is used. No auxiliary numerical computation is required for this proof. The PDF was compiled and every page visually inspected.

This problem was developed by one agent and received a separate adversarial self-review pass; no independent review of this proof is claimed. Exact logs and file hashes are included.

## Contents

Only `solutions/00000004227/gaochengzhecpu_submission_20261010224243/` is added: LaTeX source, PDF, complete Lean project, exact bilingual source, auxiliary code, reproduction instructions and verification records.

The source was checked at upstream `9b795e7a94a6076e49a65a6489e1caf9153abd23` and is checked again immediately before PR creation. AI-assisted submission by **gaochengzhecpu**.

issues.title: Disprove conjecture 00000001680: at the connectivity threshold, random geometric graphs have treewidth ≥ c·log n, not O(√(log n / log log n))
issues.body:
- **Claim refuted.** tw = Θ(√(log n / log log n)) for random geometric graphs at the connectivity threshold. The upper half O(·) fails deterministically, which refutes the Θ claim; the (true, weaker) lower half is not addressed.
- **Setting.** At least n/2 points anywhere in a box [−L,L]² (covers the unit square, the unit disk and the binomial model; Poisson on the event N ≥ n/2), Euclidean distance, any radius r > 0 with n·r² ≥ c₀·log n for any fixed c₀ > 0.
- **Grid argument.** Squares of side r/2 give O(n/log n) cells; some cell holds ≥ c·log n points, pairwise within distance r: a clique.
- **Treewidth.** The standard tree-decomposition definition (a finite Mathlib `IsTree`, vertex and edge coverage, connected node sets per vertex; tw = min over decompositions of largest bag − 1). The Helly property of subtrees puts every clique in one bag, so ω ≤ tw + 1, hence log n ≤ (64L²/c₀ + 4)(tw + 1) for every placement.
- **Result.** For every constant C and all n ≥ N(C), tw > C·√(log n / log log n) for every placement; so the event "tw ≤ C·√(log n / log log n)" has probability 0 under any distribution (`prob_upper_bound_eq_zero`). The bound also holds for every supergraph of the unit-disk graph (e.g. the torus graph).
- **Context.** Mitsche–Perarnau (STACS 2012, retrieved Dagstuhl abstract): tw = Θ(r√n) in [0,√n]², i.e. Θ(√(n log n)) at the connectivity threshold.
- **Main theorem.** `C1680.treewidth_not_upper_bound`.
- **Lean.** Lean 4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1, 425 lines. Axioms: only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. No `sorry`, no `native_decide`.

**Contents of `solutions/00000001680/Jackmeson1_submission_20261005173059/`:** `proof.tex` / `proof.pdf` (report), `lean/` (Lean 4 / Mathlib v4.33.1 project), `conjecture.md` (exact bilingual text), `SEMANTIC_REVIEW.md` (independent pre-submission model review; not the maintainers' review), `verification/` (fresh build log, axiom audit, SHA-256).

**Lean:** main theorems `C1680.treewidth_not_upper_bound`, `C1680.prob_upper_bound_eq_zero`. No `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` or added `axiom`; all depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Reproduce with `cd lean && lake exe cache get && lake build && lake env lean Axioms.lean`.

**Eligibility:** checked right before opening: no solution folder for 00000001680 on `main`, no competing open pull request, unsolved in `metadata.csv`. Only this submission folder is added.

issues.title: Disproved conjecture 00000003996: The selected Ramsey diagonal is satisfiable beyond every threshold
issues.body:
<!-- tlmc:idealistichacker:00000003996 -->

# Disproof of 00000003996: satisfiable Ramsey diagonals beyond every threshold

For every threshold K, the proof constructs k>=K and an actual red/blue coloring of
the complete graph on k^2 vertices with no monochromatic k-clique. Its standard Ramsey
CNF is satisfiable, so ordinary resolution has NOrefutation of any finite length.
This contradicts the necessary eventual-refutability premise of the stated matching
finite upper bound at n=k^2. It does NOT refute the lower bound alone or Ramsey theorem.

## Actual Infinite Family And Formal Bridges

The actual C5 graph and its complement have clique sizes at most2. The recursive
word graphs on Words(0)=Unit and Words(t+1)=Fin5 x Words(t) have5^t actual vertices.
All red and blue clique sizes are at most2^t by a proved image/fiber counting induction.
For t>=2, (2^t+1)^2<=5^t. A genuine finite injection and SimpleGraph.comap yield
actual graphs on Fin(k_t^2), k_t=2^t+1, with both colors CliqueFree(k_t).
These parameters exceed every threshold. No finite k=4 example stands in for asymptotics.

CNF.lean generates the actual standard Ramsey clauses over the COMPLETE graph's
unordered nonloop edges, taking both blocking clauses for EVERYk-vertex subset.
Actual graph assignments satisfy every clause. General ordinary resolution and
weakening soundness exclude the empty clause, without bounding proof length.
Conjecture3996.necessary_finite_upper_bound_false in Main.lean proves the CLOSED
negation; actual_diagonal_counterexamples exhibits actual graph, both clique-free
properties, assignment and no-refutation beyond every threshold.

All24 public theorem transitive axioms are audited in Check.lean, not just final
theorems or an assigned Boolean. Both unchanged source languages and exact Git/raw
SHA256 identities are retained in source.md and submission.json.

## Reproduction

Use Python3.11+, Git and exactly pinned Lean4.33.1:

```text
python -X utf8 reproduce.py --repo /path/to/The-Last-Math-Competition --lake /path/to/lean4.33.1/bin/lake
```

Default mode updates the portable pinned Git dependencies, verifies every actual
HEAD/origin/clean tracked source, clean-builds this OWNproject with warnings as errors
and audits all theorem axioms. Exact physical checkouts can use explicit --skip-update
after the same verification. Shared caches/path substitutions/tool binaries are not
part of the submission. Actual main.pdf is built from main.tex using Tectonic0.15.0
and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0, and the release validator rebuilds and compares its bytes.

Finite regressions check every C5 triple and all53130 five-subsets of its lexicographic
square. They are supplemental samples, not the all-t/all-threshold/all-clause proofs.
The restriction embedding uses standard Classical.choice from proved finite cardinality;
no computed lexicographic initial segment or exact chosen graph enumeration is claimed.

## Interpretation And Limits

This uses the standard two-EDGE-color Ramsey counterexample CNF and ordinary resolution.
Any finite asymptotic matching upper bound on the selected diagonal must provide
refutations eventually; that weaker necessary condition already fails. Merely assigning
infinite minimal length to a satisfiable CNF does not rescue a FINITEupper bound.
Adding a condition n>=R(k,k) or an unspecified unsatisfiable subsequence changes the source.
The lower bound alone, optimal Ramsey numbers and other proof systems are not assessed.
Finite DAG/listed proofs unroll to inductive proof trees as a paper argument, not an
additional general Lean DAG theorem. statement-alignment.md maps the exact scope.

AI-assisted coordinator/CNF/integration and separate Curie family implementation,
followed by a different independent Agent reviewer. No human expert endorsement,
affiliation, first-solve credit, award or organizer acceptance is claimed.


## Automated release verification
Source Git blob: `4afb4a31e851c0f313914e6b68b82ca0a9ab3d64`. Content SHA-256: `2b919eef45a9018a888ca60c01fb63aa716426b4f0641ad1922ce180e7d458e9`.
Independent review, exact reproduction, pinned Lean build, theorem axiom audit and actual LaTeX rebuild passed locally.
AI-assisted submission by idealistichacker; no affiliation claimed. This is a review request, not a claim of acceptance.
